overview: Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke hosted a community update to announce several municipal grants and public health initiatives. Key highlights included a significant grant for social responsibility programs and the donation of medical equipment for local schools and sports fields.

items.title: Medford Community Cable Station Opening
items.summary: Mayor Burke announced the opening of the new Medford Community Cable Station facility, which will be utilized by both the public and Medford High School students.

items.title: Armstrong Ambulance AED Donation
items.summary: Armstrong Ambulance donated 16 automated external defibrillators (AEDs) to the city to be distributed among athletic fields and schools.

items.title: Cummings Foundation Grant for CCSR
items.summary: The Medford Public Schools received a $100,000 grant from the Cummings Foundation to support the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility (CCSR).

items.title: Opioid Prevention Initiatives and Recovery Coach
items.summary: The Board of Health introduced a new health and safety guide for parents and the Mayor announced a budget proposal for a full-time recovery coach to combat opioid addiction.

items.title: Attorney General Health Curriculum Grant
items.summary: The school department was awarded an $18,000 grant from the Attorney General's office to fund social-emotional and decision-making curricula in elementary and middle schools.

items.title: Vocational Services Regionalization Grant
items.summary: A $45,000 grant was announced to fund regional planning with Everett Public Schools and the installation of LED lighting in vocational workshops by students.

items.title: Summer Recreation and Farmers Market
items.summary: The Mayor highlighted the launch of the summer recreation guide, the transition to a full-time recreation department, and the seasonal reopening of the Farmers Market.
